questions.question: What is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by all 12, 15 and 20?
questions.solution:
For the numbers 12, 15, and 20 →

 
 

 Number
 12
 15
 20
 
 

 Factors
 2 × 2 × 3
 3 × 5
 2 × 2 × 5
 
 

**
The prime factor 2 appears a maximum of two times (in 12 and 20).

The prime factor 3 appears a maximum of one time (in 12 and 15).

The prime factor 5 appears a maximum of one time (in 15 and 20).

Calculation:

LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5

LCM = 4 × 3 × 5

LCM = 12 × 5 = 60

The smallest positive integer divisible by 12, 15, and 20 is 60.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 1**”.

questions.question: A person has ₹7600 in the denominations of ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, and ₹200 notes. The number of notes of each denomination is equal. Find the total number of notes.
questions.solution:
Let the **number of notes** of each denomination be **x**.

The total value of the notes is determined by multiplying each denomination by the count **x** and then summing them up.

Total value = (10 × x) + (20 × x) + (50 × x) + (100 × x) + (200 × x)

Total value = (10 + 20 + 50 + 100 + 200) × x

Total value = 380 × x

**According to the problem:**

Total amount = **₹7600**

380 × x = 7600

x = 7600 / 380

**x = 20**

So, the person has **20 notes** of each denomination.

Total number of notes = 5 × x

Total number of notes = 5 × 20 = 100

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

questions.question: Which schedule of the Constitution specifies the division of powers between union and states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7th Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **7th Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** provides the framework for the **division of powers** between the **Union Government** and the **State Governments**.
 
• It implements **Article 246** of the Constitution, which deals with the legislative competence of the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures**.
 
• The schedule is divided into three lists: **List I (Union List)**, **List II (State List)**, and **List III (Concurrent List)**.
 
• The **Union List** currently contains **100 subjects** (originally 97), including critical matters of national importance such as **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Railways**, and **Currency**.
 
• The **State List** comprises **61 subjects** (originally 66) like **Public Order**, **Police**, **Public Health**, and **Sanitation**, over which states have exclusive jurisdiction.
 
• The **Concurrent List** has **52 subjects** (originally 47) including **Education**, **Forests**, and **Criminal Law**, where both the Union and States can make laws, with the **Union law** prevailing in case of conflict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **5th Schedule**

 
 
• Contains provisions relating to the administration and control of **Scheduled Areas** and **Scheduled Tribes** in any state except the four North-Eastern states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
 
 
 
• **9th Schedule**
 
 
• Introduced by the **1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951**, to protect land reform laws and other statutes from **judicial review** on the grounds of violation of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **10th Schedule**
 
 
• Known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, it was added by the **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**, specifying grounds for disqualification of members of legislative bodies due to defection.

questions.question: The oath of office to the governor is administered by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice of High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Every **Governor** and every person discharging the functions of the Governor must make and subscribe to an oath or affirmation before entering their office as per **Article 159** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The oath is administered in the presence of the **Chief Justice** of the **High Court** that exercises jurisdiction over that particular State.
 
• In the event that the **Chief Justice** is unavailable or the position is vacant, the **senior-most Judge** of that **High Court** who is currently available performs the duty of administering the oath.
 
• The specific format of the oath requires the Governor to swear to faithfully execute the office and to **preserve, protect, and defend** the Constitution and the law to the best of their ability.
 
• This constitutional requirement ensures that the **Head of the State Executive** is formally bound to the legal framework of the state and the **Union of India** before assuming any official duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President of India**

 
 
• According to **Article 155**, the **President** is the authority responsible for the **appointment** of the Governor by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• The Governor holds office during the **pleasure of the President** as stipulated in **Article 156**.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**
 
 
• The **Governor** administers the oath of office and secrecy to the **Chief Minister** and the **Council of Ministers** under **Article 164**.
 
• The Chief Minister serves as the **head of the government** at the state level, whereas the Governor is the **nominal executive head**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility and Tenure**
 
 
• To be eligible for the post of Governor under **Article 157**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and have completed **35 years of age**.
 
• The normal tenure of a Governor is **five years**, but they can resign earlier by addressing a letter to the **President**.

questions.question: Which part of India experiences the highest rainfall due to the monsoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mawsynram, Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mawsynram** is a small village located in the **East Khasi Hills** district of **Meghalaya**, positioned at an altitude of approximately **1,400 meters** above sea level.
 
• It is globally recognized as the **wettest place on Earth**, holding the **Guinness World Record** for receiving an average annual rainfall of about **11,872 millimeters**.
 
• The high precipitation is primarily caused by the **Bay of Bengal branch** of the **Southwest Monsoon**, which carries vast amounts of moisture from the sea toward the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The region features a unique **funnel-shaped topography** formed by the **Khasi Hills**, which traps moisture-laden clouds and forces them to rise abruptly.
 
• This forced ascent, known as the **orographic effect**, causes the air to cool rapidly and condense, leading to heavy and persistent rainfall during the monsoon months from **June to September**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cherrapunji (Sohra)**

 
 
• Located just **15 kilometers** from Mawsynram, it was previously the world record holder for rainfall and still holds historical records for the highest rainfall in a single month and year.
 
 
 
• **Kerala Coast**
 
 
• This region marks the **onset of the monsoon** in India, receiving the first rains of the **Arabian Sea branch** around **June 1st**, though its total annual volume is less than the northeastern plateau.
 
 
 
• **Western Rajasthan**
 
 
• This is an **arid region** because the **Aravalli Range** is oriented parallel to the path of the monsoon winds, providing no barrier to force the clouds upward for precipitation.
 
 
 
• **Konkan Coast**
 
 
• Situated on the windward side of the **Western Ghats**, it receives heavy rainfall (over **3,000 mm**), but the coastal barrier is less effective at trapping clouds compared to the Khasi Hills.

questions.question: "Ghare-Baire" (The Home and the World), which critiques the Swadeshi Movement, was written by which Bengali literateur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghare-Baire**, translated as **The Home and the World**, is a landmark novel published in **1916** by the Nobel laureate **Rabindranath Tagore**.
 
• The narrative is set against the backdrop of the **Swadeshi Movement**, which emerged following the **Partition of Bengal** in **1905** by **Lord Curzon**.
 
• The story explores the conflict between traditionalism and modern radicalism through three main characters: **Bimala** (representing India), **Nikhil** (representing rationalism and global humanism), and **Sandip** (representing fiery, divisive nationalism).
 
• Through **Nikhil**, Tagore critiques the **Swadeshi Movement** for its coercive nature and the potential for communal disharmony, emphasizing that moral principles should not be sacrificed for political ends.
 
• The novel is significant for its **psychological depth** and its use of three distinct first-person perspectives to reflect the internal struggles of its protagonists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**:

 
 
• He was an iconic Bengali novelist best known for **Anandamath** (1882), which featured the hymn **Vande Mataram**.
 
• His work largely focused on **historical romances** and the **nationalistic awakening** of India.
 
 
 
• **Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay**:
 
 
• A prolific writer who focused on the **social issues** of rural Bengal and the plight of the marginalized.

questions.question:
The axial tilt of Uranus is about 98°, meaning it rotates almost on its side.

What effect does this have on Uranus' seasons?

__
 
• The axial tilt of **Uranus** is approximately **97.77 degrees** (often rounded to 98 degrees), which means its axis of rotation is nearly parallel to its **orbital plane**.
 
• Because of this unique orientation, **Uranus** rotates essentially on its side, unlike other planets whose axes are more or less perpendicular to their orbits.
 
• This extreme tilt results in the **Sun** shining directly over each pole for a massive portion of the planet's year; since Uranus takes **84 Earth years** to orbit the Sun, each pole experiences **21 years of continuous sunlight** followed by **21 years of total darkness**.
 
• These conditions lead to the most **dramatic seasonal variations** observed in the solar system, where sunlight distribution shifts from being concentrated entirely at one pole to being distributed along the equator during **equinoxes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric Temperature**: Despite the extreme seasonal sunlight, **Uranus** holds the title of the **coldest planet** in the solar system, with minimum temperatures reaching 49 Kelvin (−224 degrees Celsius).
 
• **Rotation Direction**: **Uranus** exhibits **retrograde rotation**, meaning it spins in the opposite direction to its orbital motion, a trait shared only with **Venus**.
 
• **Magnetic Field**: The planet's magnetic field is unusual because it does not originate from the geometric center and is tilted at an angle of **59 degrees** from the axis of rotation, further complicating its **magnetosphere** interactions during different seasons.
 
• **Equinox Dynamics**: During its equinoxes, the planet experiences a rapid **day-night cycle** of about 17 hours, but during **solstices**, the side facing the Sun remains in **permanent daylight** for decades.

questions.question:
The light from a star 100 light years away takes about 100 years to reach Earth.

How long will the star appear to us after it explodes (if it explodes now)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In 100 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **light-year** is a unit of astronomical distance representing the total distance that **light** travels in a vacuum in one Julian year (approximately 365.25 days).
 
• Light travels at a finite, constant speed of approximately **299,792,458 meters per second** (commonly rounded to **3 × 10⁸ m/s**).
 
• If a celestial object, such as a **star**, is located **100 light-years** away from **Earth**, it means the electromagnetic radiation (light) emitted by that star must traverse a distance that requires exactly **100 years** of travel time.
 
• When a star **explodes**, the visual information and energy from the event begin traveling outward at the **speed of light**; therefore, there is a time lag between the physical event and its **observation** on Earth.
 
• Since the distance is 100 light-years, the light from an explosion occurring **'now'** will not reach an observer's eyes until **100 years** have passed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lookback Time:**

 
 
• In **astronomy**, because light takes time to travel, looking further into space is equivalent to looking further back in **time**.
 
• We never see the universe as it exists at this exact moment, but rather as it was when the light was first **emitted**.
 
 
 
• **Scale of a Light-Year:**
 
 
• One **light-year** is approximately **9.46 trillion kilometers** (9.46 × 10¹² km).
 
• For context, light from the **Sun** takes about **8 minutes and 20 seconds** to reach Earth, meaning we see the Sun as it was over eight minutes ago.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Light Constraint:**
 
 
• According to **Einstein's Theory of Relativity**, nothing can travel faster than the **speed of light (c)**; hence, no signal or information about the explosion can reach Earth **immediately** or in **1 year**.

questions.question: Bone belongs to which category of animal tissues?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Connective tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bone is a specialized form of **skeletal connective tissue** that constitutes the majority of the **endoskeleton** in vertebrates, providing structural support and shape.
 
• It is distinguished by a hard, non-pliable **extracellular matrix** that is heavily impregnated with **calcium salts** (primarily hydroxyapatite) and **collagen fibers**, which provide both compressive strength and tensile flexibility.
 
• The cellular components of bone are called **osteocytes**, which reside in small spaces known as **lacunae** within the calcified matrix.
 
• In long bones, the tissue is organized into **osteons** or **Haversian systems**, consisting of concentric layers of matrix called **lamellae** surrounding a central canal that contains **blood vessels** and **nerve fibers**.
 
• Functionally, bones protect delicate organs (like the brain and heart), facilitate **locomotion** by acting as levers for muscles, and serve as a site for **hematopoiesis** (blood cell formation) within the **bone marrow**.
 
• Bones also function as a metabolic reservoir for minerals, regulating the systemic balance of **calcium** and **phosphorus** in the blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epithelial tissue**

 
 
• Forms the continuous protective layer on the body surface and the lining of internal organs and **glands**.
 
• Cells are tightly packed with minimal **intercellular matrix** and rest on a **basement membrane**.
 
 
 
• **Muscular tissue**
 
 
• Specialized for contraction and movement through the interaction of **actin** and **myosin** proteins.
 
• Includes **skeletal muscle** (striated and voluntary), **smooth muscle** (non-striated and involuntary), and **cardiac muscle**.
 
 
 
• **Nervous tissue**
 
 
• Composed of **neurons** (excitable cells) and **neuroglia** (supporting cells) that form the **brain**, spinal cord, and nerves.
 
• Facilitates rapid communication by transmitting electrical impulses throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Other Specialized Connective Tissues**
 
 
• **Cartilage**: Has a solid but pliable matrix made of **chondroitin salts**; it provides flexibility at joints and in the respiratory tract.
 
• **Blood**: A fluid connective tissue containing **plasma**, **red blood cells**, **white blood cells**, and **platelets**, primarily used for transport.

questions.question: What is the primary function of chloroplasts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are specialized **double-membrane** organelles found primarily in the **mesophyll cells** of plant leaves and in eukaryotic algae.
 
• The primary function is to perform **photosynthesis**, a process where light energy is converted into chemical energy in the form of **glucose**.
 
• They contain the green pigment **chlorophyll**, which is essential for absorbing light energy (photons) from the sun.
 
• The internal structure consists of a fluid matrix called the **stroma** and a system of membrane-bound sacs called **thylakoids**, which are stacked to form **grana**.
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in two stages: the **light-dependent reactions** (taking place in the thylakoid membranes) and the **light-independent reactions** or **Calvin Cycle** (occurring in the stroma).
 
• The overall chemical reaction can be represented as: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**:

 
 
• Often termed the **powerhouse of the cell**, they are responsible for **ATP production** through **cellular respiration**, unlike chloroplasts which produce food.
 
 
 
• **Amyloplasts**:
 
 
• These are non-pigmented organelles (**leucoplasts**) dedicated to the **storage of starch** granules in specialized plant tissues like roots and tubers.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**:
 
 
• These are the molecular machines responsible for **protein synthesis** by translating messenger RNA into polypeptide chains.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**:
 
 
• Chloroplasts possess their own circular **DNA** and **70S ribosomes**, suggesting they originated from ancient **cyanobacteria** that entered into a symbiotic relationship with eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: Area of a rhombus is 840 square cm. Side of the rhombus is 29 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of its diagonals?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **rhombus**, the relation between the **side** (a), **area** (A), and the **sum of diagonals** (d₁+d₂) is given by:

(d₁ + d₂)² = 4a² + 4A

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = 4 × 29² + 4 × 840

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = 3364 + 3360 = 6724

⇒ d₁ + d₂ = √6724 = 82 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 82 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Area** of the **rhombus** = 840 cm²

⇒ **Side** of the **rhombus** (a) = 29 cm

**Formula used:**

⇒ **Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

⇒ **Side**² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)² ⇒ 4a² = d₁² + d₂²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebce8c8c8dd3b94d53479e86e9f661d875372e0acdf4b70f5860eb90fd393f5a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = 840

⇒ d₁ × d₂ = 1680

⇒ 2 × d₁ × d₂ = 3360

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 4 × (Side)² = 4 × 29²

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 4 × 841 = 3364

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = 3364 + 3360 = 6724

⇒ d₁ + d₂ = √6724

⇒ d₁ + d₂ = 82 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 82 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

All sides are equal and opposite sides are parallel. The **diagonals** bisect each other at 90°.

Perimeter of Rhombus

The **perimeter** of a rhombus is given by 4 × Side (a).

Relationship between Diagonals and Side

The **side** and **diagonals** are related by the formula 4a² = d₁² + d₂², derived from the **Pythagoras theorem**.

Angle Properties

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple of 3/5, 4/15 and 8/25?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of fractions, use the formula:

**LCM** = **LCM of Numerators** ÷ **HCF of Denominators**

Numerators: 3, 4, 8 ⇒ **LCM** = 24

Denominators: 5, 15, 25 ⇒ **HCF** = 5

Required Result = 24/5

**∴ The correct answer is 24/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Fractions:** 3/5, 4/15, and 8/25

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c82885e38d6130919321f21a90bf7ac77ffbd05a011099c224a813759f8359e.png] 

**Detailed Calculation:**

⇒ **Numerators** are 3, 4, and 8. The **Least Common Multiple** of 3, 4, and 8 is 24 (since 24 is the smallest number divisible by 3, 4, and 8).

⇒ **Denominators** are 5, 15, and 25. The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of 5, 15, and 25 is 5 (since 5 is the largest number that divides 5, 15, and 25 exactly).

⇒ Applying the **Fraction LCM Rule**:

⇒ LCM = 24 ÷ 5 = 24/5

**∴ The correct answer is 24/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

The formula to find the HCF of fractions is HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators).

Simplified Form Rule

Always ensure the fractions are in their **lowest terms** (simplest form) before applying the LCM or HCF formulas.

Product of Numbers Property

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 5 and their Least Common Multiple is 120. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 3 : 5. Let the numbers be **3x** and **5x**.

**LCM** of (3x, 5x) = 15x.

Given 15x = 120 ⇒ x = 8.

**Sum** of the numbers = (3 + 5) × x = 8 × 8 = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio = 3 : 5, **LCM** = 120.

**Formula Used:** LCM = Product of ratio parts × **HCF** (when ratio is in its simplest form).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df42a79bf5a7795e3170a2c35af855035b924eb38505526d1a4f6a2a6a6c5884.png] 

⇒ Let the two numbers be **3x** and **5x**.

⇒ LCM of 3x and 5x = 120

⇒ 15x = 120

⇒ x = 120 ÷ 15 = 8

⇒ **First number** = 3 × 8 = 24

⇒ **Second number** = 5 × 8 = 40

⇒ **Sum** of the numbers = 24 + 40 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: A × B = HCF × LCM.

Ratio and Multiples

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their HCF is **H**, then the numbers are **aH** and **bH**, and their LCM is **abH**.

Coprime Numbers

If two numbers are **coprime** (HCF = 1), then their **LCM** is simply the product of the numbers.

questions.question: What is the value of 30 percent of 20 percent of 2/5 of 4500?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine the **percentages** first: 30% × 20% = 6% (or 0.06).

Calculate **2/5 of 4500**: 4500 ÷ 5 × 2 = 1800.

Find 6% of the result: 6/100 × 1800 = 6 × 18 = 108.

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total value = 4500, Fractions/Percentages = 2/5, 20%, 30%

**Formula:** Value = (P₁/100) × (P₂/100) × (Fraction) × Number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a2f142b28bd6e551319ce30829a495186ebc835bc8387437b34c5e2cbed0140.png] 

⇒ Result = 30/100 × 20/100 × 2/5 × 4500

⇒ Result = 3/10 × 1/5 × 2/5 × 4500

⇒ Result = 3/10 × 1/5 × 1800

⇒ Result = 3/10 × 360

⇒ Result = 3 × 36

⇒ Result = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentages

When calculating multiple percentages of a number, you can multiply the **decimal equivalents** directly: a% of b% of X = (a × b / 10000) × X.

Fraction-to-Percentage Conversion

Common fractions like **2/5** are equal to 40%. Converting fractions to percentages can often simplify the mental math.

BODMAS in Percentage

The word **'of'** in mathematical problems always signifies **multiplication** and should be solved sequentially or simultaneously in such expressions.

questions.question: If A = 2X and B = 5X, then B is what percent of A?

To find **B as a percent of A**, use the ratio: **(5 ÷ 2) × 100**. Calculation: **2.5 × 100 = 250**. **∴ The correct answer is 250 percent.**

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 10 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 20 percent. What will be the new profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are both increased or decreased by the same percentage, the **Profit Percentage** remains unchanged.

Initial Profit = 10% ⇒ Ratio CP : SP = 100 : 110 = 10 : 11.

Both values are decreased by 20%, which means they are multiplied by a factor of 0.8.

New Ratio = (10 × 0.8) : (11 × 0.8) = 8 : 8.8 = 10 : 11.

Since the ratio remains 10 : 11, the **profit percentage** remains 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial profit percentage = 10%

Reduction in **Cost Price (CP)** = 20%

Reduction in **Selling Price (SP)** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc020115b31d552488f1668a94ea76ef5c88046ae4e01598594b727e6fed9fc0.png] ⇒ Let the **Initial Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100 ⇒ Since Profit is 10%, **Initial Selling Price (SP₁)** = 100 + 10 = 110 ⇒ **New Cost Price (CP₂)** = 100 − 20% of 100 = 100 − 20 = 80 ⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 110 − 20% of 110 = 110 − 22 = 88 ⇒ **New Profit** = SP₂ − CP₂ = 88 − 80 = 8 ⇒ **New Profit Percentage** = (New Profit ÷ New CP) × 100 ⇒ New Profit % = (8 ÷ 80) × 100 = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Scaling on Percentages

If all terms in a ratio (like CP and SP) are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero constant, the ratio remains equivalent, and the resulting percentage (Profit or Loss) remains unchanged.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price can also be calculated as **Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100**. Profit is always calculated on CP, while Discount is calculated on MP.

Net Profit after Successive Changes

If CP changes by x% and SP changes by y%, the new profit percentage must be found by calculating the new absolute values of CP and SP individually.

questions.question: Cost price of 20 articles is Rs. 260. Selling price of 25 articles is Rs. 260. What is the profit/loss percentage? (Cost price of all the articles is same. Selling price of all the articles is same.)

When the total amount is constant, the ratio of prices is the inverse of the ratio of articles.

Ratio of **Cost Price** : **Selling Price** = 25 : 20 = 5 : 4

Loss = 5 − 4 = 1 unit

Loss % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price** (CP) of 20 articles = ₹260

**Selling Price** (SP) of 25 articles = ₹260

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

**Loss Percentage** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1caacd3e41affdc8d8661764599cd38d684665e1b2a7e3f4b2a6afea52ceb992.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price** of 1 article = 260 ÷ 20 = ₹13

⇒ **Selling Price** of 1 article = 260 ÷ 25 = ₹10.4

⇒ Loss = 13 − 10.4 = ₹2.6

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (2.6 ÷ 13) × 100

**∴ The correct answer is 20% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Loss occurs when CP > SP. Both are always calculated on the CP unless stated otherwise.

Relationship Formula

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit or Loss %) ÷ 100. This is the direct way to find SP from CP and percentage.

Inverse Variation in Articles

If CP of 'x' articles = SP of 'y' articles, then Profit or Loss % = (x − y) ÷ y × 100. Positive result is profit, negative is loss.

questions.question: Four numbers are in the ratio of 2 : 4 : 5 : 7. Sum of these numbers is 54. What is the difference between the largest and smallest number?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total units in **Ratio** = 2 + 4 + 5 + 7 = 18 units

Given **Sum**: 18 units = 54 ⇒ 1 unit = 3

Difference between **Largest** (7) and **Smallest** (2) = 7 − 2 = 5 units

Required Difference = 5 × 3 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Ratio of four numbers = 2 : 4 : 5 : 7

Sum of numbers = 54

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1991c65caa37c05bcd9450f5f97eaeab41c5b0086215530fec28d7202e8fd076.png] 

Let the four numbers be 2x, 4x, 5x, and 7x.

Sum of numbers = 2x + 4x + 5x + 7x = 54

⇒ 18x = 54

⇒ x = 54 ÷ 18

⇒ x = 3

Smallest number = 2x = 2 × 3 = 6

Largest number = 7x = 7 × 3 = 21

Difference = 21 − 6 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportional Parts

To divide a quantity into parts based on a ratio a : b : c, the individual parts are (a/Sum) × Total, (b/Sum) × Total, etc., where Sum = a + b + c.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b). It is the value x such that a : x = x : b.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios a : b and c : d is found by multiplying corresponding terms: (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 5000. The cost price of the article is Rs. 3000. It is sold at a profit of 25 percent. What is the discount percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Selling Price (SP)** = 125% of **Cost Price (CP)** = 1.25 × 3000 = ₹3750

**Discount** = **Marked Price (MP)** − SP = 5000 − 3750 = ₹1250

**Discount Percentage** = (Discount / MP) × 100 = (1250 / 5000) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹5000

**Cost Price (CP)** = ₹3000

**Profit Percentage** = 25%

**Formula Used:**

1. **Selling Price (SP)** = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100

2. **Discount Percentage** = [(MP − SP) / MP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52fb45fec192091dd4e3f96c1c9d2543ccff9e4c48206ac2b67194906ff75c0f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 3000 × (125 / 100)

⇒ SP = ₹3750

⇒ Discount = MP − SP = 5000 − 3750 = ₹1250

⇒ Discount Percentage = (1250 / 5000) × 100

⇒ Discount Percentage = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by: MP / CP = (100 + Profit %) / (100 − Discount %).

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the extra price added to CP to get MP: Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the net discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: What is the fourth proportion of 8, 10 and 16?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **fourth proportion** (x) of three numbers a, b, and c is calculated using the formula: x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Given: a = 8, b = 10, and c = 16.

x = (10 × 16) ÷ 8

x = 160 ÷ 8 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three numbers: 8, 10, and 16.

**Formula Used:**

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in **proportion**, then a : b :: c : d, which means (a ÷ b) = (c ÷ d) or **Product of Extremes = Product of Means** (a × d = b × c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b68e9b4cafe7371078426a66ed1293b5ef1b756a5c5e5f7e17ccccaf4aaee40e.png] 

Let the fourth proportion be **x**.

⇒ 8 : 10 :: 16 : x

⇒ 8 ÷ 10 = 16 ÷ x

⇒ 8 × x = 10 × 16

⇒ 8x = 160

⇒ x = 160 ÷ 8

⇒ x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportion

The mean proportion between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportion

The third proportion of two numbers a and b is the value x such that a : b :: b : x, which is x = b² ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Three quantities a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a : b = b : c.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Mysophobia** is defined as an intense, pathological, and irrational **fear of dirt**, **germs**, and **contamination**.

• The term was first introduced to medical literature by **William Alexander Hammond** in **1879** when he was describing a specific manifestation of **Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD)** characterized by a patient's need for constant handwashing.

• Etymologically, the word is derived from the Greek words **mysos**, meaning **uncleanness** or **impurity**, and **phobos**, meaning **fear**.

• Individuals with **Mysophobia**, often called **germaphobes**, frequently engage in ritualistic behaviors such as **excessive cleaning**, wearing **gloves** or masks in public, and the compulsive use of **sanitizers** to avoid **bacteria** and **viruses**.

• Severe cases can lead to significant social isolation, as the individual may avoid public transport, restaurants, or physical contact (like **handshakes**) to mitigate the perceived risk of **infection**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Hemophobia**:

• This refers to the intense **fear of blood**, whether it is seeing their own blood, the blood of others, or even images of blood.

• Similar to **Trypanophobia**, it is distinct from other phobias because it often triggers a **vasovagal syncope** rather than a typical fight-or-flight anxiety response.

• **Dentophobia**:

• It is the overwhelming **fear of dentists** or **dental treatments**.

• To convert a sentence from **Passive Voice** to **Active Voice**, the **Object** of the passive sentence ('the council') must become the **Subject** of the active sentence.

• The original sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense**, as indicated by the auxiliary verb **are** followed by the past participle **organised**, and the adverbial phrase **every summer** which signifies a habitual action.

• In the **Active Voice** structure for the **Simple Present Tense**, the verb follows the formula: **Subject + V1 (s/es) + Object**.

• Since the new subject **the council** is a **singular collective noun**, the verb must take the **-s** suffix, changing **organised** back to its base form **organises**.

• The phrase **every summer to promote international understanding** remains as a modifier to provide context regarding frequency and purpose.

 **Additional Information__**

• Comparison with other options:

• **Simple Past Tense**: Option 2 uses **organised**, which would be the active form of **were organised**. It indicates a completed action in the past rather than a recurring habit.

• **Simple Future Tense**: Option 4 uses **will organise**, which refers to an action that will happen later. The passive equivalent would be **will be organised**.

__
 
• The provided sentence 'Let the work not be delayed any further' is in the **Passive Voice** and is categorized as an **Imperative Sentence** expressing a command or instruction.
 
• In **Imperative Sentences**, the passive structure 'Let + object + not + be + Past Participle (V3)' is converted into the active structure 'Do not (Don't) + Base Verb (V1) + object'.
 
• In this specific case, **'the work'** acts as the object, and **'delayed'** is the past participle form of the verb **'delay'**.
 
• When shifting to the **Active Voice**, the hidden subject **'You'** is understood but typically omitted in imperative commands. The sentence starts with the **negative auxiliary** 'Don't' followed by the **base form** of the verb 'delay'.
 
• The phrase 'any further' remains an **adverbial adjunct** at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning and intensity of the instruction.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voice Transformation Rules:**
 
 
• **Positive Imperative:** Active (V1 + Object) becomes Passive (Let + Object + be + V3). For example, 'Finish the task' becomes 'Let the task be finished'.

• A **simple infinitive** (to reduce) usually refers to the same time as the main verb or a future time. A **perfect infinitive** (to have reduced) refers to a time earlier than the main verb.
